name: find
description: Look up the user's named records: bills, receivables (money owed to them), set-asides, budgets, budget groups, installment plans and accounts (with balances, credit limits and open statements). Use it for "a named record and its details" and to get the id an edit, delete or settlement needs. The query matches on all its words in any order ("meralco aug", "bpi card"); a month name in it sets the month. Every reply starts with a status: found (exactly one match comes back with ALL its fields — paid date, paid amount, account, note, linked ledger entry, series — so do not look it up again), ambiguous (several matched: ask which, or narrow the query), not_found (nearest names and matches in other months are listed: never invent an id), or error (fix the call as it says). Which tool answers what: a named record → find; rows in a period → findTransactions; a figure a screen shows → getView; a sum or group-by no screen shows → queryFinance. Do NOT call find before adding something new: the snapshot already lists this month's records, and an unasked lookup makes the user wait.

query.description: Name or words of it, e.g. "internet", "meralco aug". Omit to list every record of the entity.

month.description: YYYY-MM for bills, receivables, set-asides, budgets and budget groups. Defaults to the current month. Ignored for installments and accounts.

name: findTransactions
description: Go through the user's ledger transactions, past or present: spending, income and transfers, with date, account, category and note. Call this ONLY when the user asks to review, audit, look up, search or list their transactions, or asks about a specific purchase or payment the snapshot does not show ("what did I spend at Grab in March", "review my August transactions", "when did I last pay Meralco"). Do NOT call it for general advice or a summary question: the snapshot already lists recent spending and each past month's biggest expenses, and an unrequested lookup makes the user wait. The rows come straight from the ledger and are as quotable as the snapshot. This answers "rows in a period"; a named bill, account or plan is find, and a total grouped by category, account or month is queryFinance.

query.description: Text to match against the description, note, category, account or who owes it, e.g. "grab". With a query and no dates, the whole history is searched.

month.description: YYYY-MM. With no query and no dates, defaults to the current month.

from.description: YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. For a range that is not one calendar month. Overrides month.

type.description: Only this direction. Omit for all.

category.description: Category NAME or part of it.

account.description: Account NAME or part of it.

limit.description: Most rows to return, newest first. Default 50, max 150. Totals always cover every match.

name: queryFinance
description: Answer a sum or group-by that no screen shows, computed from the ledger with the app's own rules: "average monthly spending since I started", "top 5 categories this year", "how much did I spend at Grab per month", "how much did I set aside in Q3". Quote its figures as they are: never add, subtract or average them yourself. A figure a screen shows (budget left, forecast, pace) comes from getView, a named record and its details from find, and the rows of a period from findTransactions. The result states the range, the months covered and what the metric counts.

metric.description: spend: real spending (no transfers, reimbursables or installment purchase records). income: real income. net: income minus spend. count: number of entries. setAside: money moved into savings pockets, less money moved out.

groupBy.description: One line per group. Default none (the total only). month lists every month in the range, including empty ones.

category.description: Category NAME or part of it.

account.description: Account NAME or part of it.

query.description: Words to match, in any order, against the description, note, category, account or who owes it, e.g. "grab".

type.description: Only this direction. Omit for all.

month.description: YYYY-MM. With no month and no dates, the whole history is used, from the first ledger entry to today.

top.description: Most groups to list, biggest first. Default 10. The total always covers every group.

average.description: Also give the average per month over the range, counting a month with no activity as 0. Use it for "average monthly …" questions.

name: addBill
description: Propose a new bill (money the user owes and will pay). Call this as soon as you have a name, an amount and a due day — do not ask permission in prose first, because calling it IS how the user is asked: they get a confirmation card and nothing is saved until they accept it.

dueDay.description: Day of the month it is due, 1-31.

isRecurring.description: True if it repeats monthly. Default false.

category.description: Expense category NAME; the client resolves it.

account.description: Preferred paying account NAME, if the user said one.

month.description: YYYY-MM. Defaults to the month being viewed.

name: addReceivable
description: Propose a new receivable (money owed TO the user, expected to come in). Call it as soon as you have a name and an amount — the confirmation card is how the user is asked, so asking in prose first only makes them wait.

name.description: Say who owes it in the name, e.g. "Mark - concert ticket". A receivable has no separate debtor field.

expectedDay.description: Day of the month it is expected, 1-31.

name: addSetAside
description: Propose setting money aside for a purpose — savings, a goal such as braces, a sinking fund. This is a transfer between the user's own accounts, never spending. Call it as soon as you have a name, an amount and a type — the confirmation card is how the user is asked, so asking in prose first only makes them wait.

destinationAccount.description: Savings account or goal NAME the money moves into.

isRecurring.description: True if set aside every month. Default false.

name: logTransactions
description: Propose one or more ledger transactions — actual money that moved (spending, income received, a transfer between the user's own accounts). Call it whenever the user asks you to log, record, add or re-log spending, including when the amounts come from earlier in this conversation ("log the oil change again"): listing the entries in prose logs nothing. Every entry joins the review list with the other changes of this step, where the user fixes anything wrong and approves; the result comes back after they answer and says exactly what was logged. Use the exact account and category NAMES from the snapshot; leave a field out rather than inventing one and the row gives the user a picker for it. Amounts are separate entries when they were separate charges (₱295 oil and ₱50 labour are two). This does NOT change entries already in the ledger — use editTransaction or deleteTransaction for that.

amount.description: In pesos, always positive. Direction comes from "type", never from a minus sign.

description.description: Short human label, e.g. "Motor oil change". Not the raw sentence.

type.description: Default outflow. "transfer" moves money between the user's own accounts and is never spending.

account.description: Account NAME the money left or entered, exactly as the snapshot spells it.

category.description: Expense/income category NAME. Omit on a transfer.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today. Never a future date.

reimbursable.description: True when the user spent it but is owed it back (a work expense, money spotted for someone).

owedBy.description: Who owes a reimbursable expense back.

expectedReimbursementDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD the money is expected back.

name: addInstallment
description: Propose a new installment purchase on a credit card, credit line or BNPL account (e.g. SPayLater, a credit card 0% plan). This logs the purchase, holds that much of the credit limit, and splits it into monthly payments billed on the account's statement. Call as soon as you have a name, total amount, credit account and number of months — the confirmation card is how the user is asked. It only goes on a credit account; a purchase paid in one go is a logTransactions entry, not an installment. If the call fails, relay the reason and ask the user rather than guessing a value.

name.description: Item or purchase description, e.g. "MacBook Pro", "Phone".

amount.description: Total purchase amount in pesos, above zero.

months.description: Number of monthly payments, at least 2, e.g. 3, 6, 12, 24. Ask the user if they did not say.

account.description: Credit card, credit line or BNPL account NAME, exactly as the snapshot spells it. May be omitted only when the user has a single credit account.

interestRate.description: MONTHLY add-on interest rate in percent: 0 for a 0% promo, 1.5 for 1.5% a month. Not an annual rate — divide a yearly rate by 12. Default 0.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD purchase date. Defaults to today. Never a future date.

name: checkAffordability
description: Run the "Can I afford it?" check: calculates whether a proposed expense or purchase fits within the user's projected month-end spare cash after all planned bills, savings, and budget allocations. Call when the user asks "Can I afford X?", "Do I have enough for Y?", or similar questions.

amount.description: Proposed purchase or expense amount in pesos.

account.description: Optional account NAME to verify spendable cash on that specific account.

name: getView
description: Read a screen's figures, labelled as the screen labels them and computed by the app exactly as the screen shows them. Use it for "a screen's figure" questions: "how much budget do I have left", "where will my cash be at the end of next month", "am I on pace", "what does the History tab say I average", "what is on my card statement", "how much do I hold for others". Quote the figures; never add or subtract them yourself. For a named record use find; for rows in a period use findTransactions; for a sum or group-by no screen shows use queryFinance.

view.description: dashboard: net worth, liquid cash, Budget Left, month-end outlook, next-month forecast. budget: spent vs budgeted, pace, every group and row. bills: pending/paid, coming up, statement line items, receivables, set-asides. ledger: month in/out/net, owed, daily average. history: averages, % saved, a month's closed summary and balances at close. accounts: every balance, held, yours, credit limit, statement/due days. installments: every plan. grocery: cart, price book, last trips.

month.description: YYYY-MM. Defaults to the current month. The dashboard shows the current month only; accounts and grocery have no month.

name: payCredit
description: Propose a payment to a credit card or line of credit (a transfer from a liquid account to a liability account, which reduces the debt owed). Call as soon as you have the credit card name and the amount — the user gets a confirmation card and nothing is saved until they accept it.

creditAccount.description: Credit card or BNPL account NAME being paid.

amount.description: Payment amount in pesos, always positive.

fromAccount.description: Funding account NAME, e.g. "BPI Savings", "GCash". Optional.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD payment date. Defaults to today.

name: markBillPaid
description: Mark an existing bill as paid for the month. Call ONLY after find returns the bill id. The user confirms on a card before the bill is marked paid.

id.description: The exact bill id from a preceding find result.

paidAmount.description: Amount paid in pesos. Omit to pay the bill's full amount.

paidDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD date it was paid. Defaults to today.

account.description: Account NAME it was paid from, if named by user.

alreadyLogged.description: True when the user says they already logged this payment in the Ledger, so no second entry is recorded. The card lets them change it.

name: markReceivableReceived
description: Mark money owed to the user as received. Call ONLY after find returns the receivable id. Settling a receivable creates the offsetting income entry in the ledger automatically. The user confirms on a card before anything is saved.

id.description: The exact receivable id from a preceding find result.

receivedAmount.description: Amount received in pesos (if partial). Defaults to full receivable amount.

receivedDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD date received. Defaults to today.

account.description: Account NAME the money landed in, e.g. "GCash", "BPI".

alreadyLogged.description: True when the user says they already logged this income in the Ledger, so no second entry is recorded. The card lets them change it.

name: fundSetAside
description: Propose funding an existing set-aside: move the money into it, the way "Set aside into" does on the Bills tab. It is a transfer between the user's own accounts, never spending. Call ONLY after find (entity setAside) returns its id. The user approves on the review list before anything moves.

id.description: The exact set-aside id from a preceding find call.

amount.description: Pesos to set aside. Omit for the allocated amount.

fromAccount.description: Account NAME the money leaves. Omit for the set-aside's own funding account.

intoAccount.description: Savings or goal account NAME it moves into. Omit for the set-aside's own destination.

name: editBill
description: Propose an edit to an existing bill (name, amount, due day, or category). Call ONLY after find (entity bill) returns the bill id. Do NOT supply an id unprompted. Nothing is saved until the user accepts the confirmation card.

id.description: The exact bill id from a preceding find call.

name: editReceivable
description: Propose an edit to an existing receivable (name, amount or expected day). Call ONLY after find (entity receivable) returns the receivable id. Nothing is saved until confirmed on the card.

id.description: The exact receivable id from a preceding find call.

name: editSetAside
description: Propose an edit to an existing set-aside (name, amount, type, or destination). Call ONLY after find (entity setAside) returns the set-aside id. Nothing is saved until confirmed.

id.description: The exact set-aside id from a preceding find call.

name: editTransaction
description: Propose editing an existing ledger transaction. Call ONLY after findTransactions returns the transaction id. The user confirms on a card before changes are applied. Do NOT use this to reverse flow direction (inflow vs outflow) — ask the user to delete and re-log instead.

id.description: The exact transaction id from a preceding findTransactions call.

amount.description: Updated amount in pesos, always positive.

name: deleteBill
description: Propose deleting an existing bill. Call ONLY after find returns the bill id. The user confirms on a card before the bill is deleted.

id.description: The exact bill id from a preceding find call.

name: deleteReceivable
description: Propose deleting an existing receivable. Call ONLY after find returns the receivable id. The user confirms on a card before deletion.

id.description: The exact receivable id from a preceding find call.

name: deleteSetAside
description: Propose deleting an existing set-aside. Call ONLY after find returns the set-aside id. The user confirms on a card before deletion.

id.description: The exact set-aside id from a preceding find call.

name: deleteTransaction
description: Propose permanently deleting a ledger transaction. Call ONLY after findTransactions returns the transaction id. The user confirms on an explicit warning card before the transaction is deleted.

id.description: The exact transaction id from a preceding findTransactions call.
